Recommended next steps

  1. Update or verify vendor backports for: PHP 8.4.24 @ /demo/php (update toward 8.4.27 or verify an equivalent vendor security backport). Restart PHP-FPM, Apache/mod_php, IIS FastCGI, or other workers that may load these builds, then confirm the serving runtime version.
  2. Identify which PHP binary or SAPI actually serves HTTP (FPM pool, Apache module, IIS handler, container entrypoint). Package and CLI versions alone are not sufficient.
  3. Review possible compromise leads (process relationships and/or webroot filesystem heuristics) against host baselines. Normal apps may launch shells; CMS uploads can look suspicious; validate before concluding. Never treat as confirmed compromise or webshell.
  4. Validate remediation by checking the active web handler version after restart, and review official guidance at https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-21-1.

Extended remediation notes

  1. URGENT: Observed installed or operator-reported PHP version below the upstream fixes. Patch all relevant running web SAPIs, not only the CLI binary. Confirm vendor backports where applicable.
  2. Immediately prioritize internet-reachable mod_php and other web-facing PHP (FPM, CGI, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed). Determine network reachability separately; this is NOT an external exposure scan.
  3. Apply upstream PHP 8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35 or your vendor's verified equivalent patches. Restart/recycle all PHP workers, pools and services; re-scan and verify the active web-serving SAPI and container images.
  4. If patching must be delayed: consider administratively enforced memory_limit=-1, conservative post_max_size and edge request bounds for CVE-2026-109618; these are incomplete risk reductions and have availability tradeoffs.
  5. For CVE-2026-109619, administratively disable session.upload_progress.enabled and restart all workers; on PHP 8.5, consider fatal_error_backtraces=0 until patched. Neither measure covers every attack path.
  6. Confirm WAF/origin access cannot be bypassed and document time-bounded restrictions if a patch cannot be deployed immediately.
  7. Preserve and review access/error logs and EDR telemetry from before patching; patched servers may already have been compromised. A clean IOC result does not rule out compromise.
  8. See official advisories: https://www.php.net/ and https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w and https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp
